findings.title: labels= silently dropped (partially or entirely) in animations whenever frame_rate*duration < sample count
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from hypertools.plot import matplotlib_backend as mb
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(50).randn(30,5), axis=0)
labels = [None]*30; labels[0], labels[15] = 'L0', 'L15'
fig, ani = hyp.plot(A, animate=True, duration=1.0, frame_rate=5, labels=labels, show=False)
print(len(mb.labels_and_points))  # 0 -- both labels silently gone
findings.expected: Both labels drawn once and visible across frames (docstring), or at minimum a UserWarning that labels were dropped.
findings.actual: labels_and_points exists: True | len: 0; returned fig annotations: [] -- and with frame_rate=20: len 1 (one label silently lost). Unit-level: _expand_labels(labels,[30],[5]) -> non-None labels=[]

findings.title: elev= and azim= are accepted, fully functional camera kwargs but have NO entry in the plot() docstring
findings.repro:
python - <<'EOF'
import inspect, hypertools as hyp
src = inspect.getdoc(hyp.plot)
print('elev' in src, 'azim :' in src)  # False False
EOF
findings.expected: Documented parameter entries for elev/azim (camera elevation/azimuth in degrees, defaults 10/-60, both backends).
findings.actual: grep of docstring lines 210-1224 for '^    elev'/'^    azim' -> no matches; runtime behavior verified working: default (elev,azim)=(10, -60); custom -> (90, 0); pixels differ (aae3d209 vs 17cb34b9)

findings.title: fmt list length is never validated: too short crashes with bare IndexError, too long is silently ignored
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0); B = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(2).randn(30,5),axis=0)
hyp.plot([A,B], ['-'], show=False)   # IndexError
hyp.plot([A,B], ['-','o',':'], show=False)  # silent
findings.expected: ValueError naming fmt=, the given length, and the required dataset count (matching parse_kwargs' message for color/marker/linestyle).
findings.actual: IndexError: list index out of range  (File hypertools/plot/plot.py, line 2333, in plot: if has_line_component(fmt[idx])) ; long list: no error/warning, extras ignored

findings.title: A single RGB(A) tuple as color= is always misinterpreted as a per-dataset list (rejected or split into float 'colors')
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0)
hyp.plot(A, color=(0.2,0.4,0.6), show=False)  # ValueError length 3 vs 1 dataset
B,C = A+1, A+2
hyp.plot([A,B,C], color=(0.9,0.4,0.1), show=False)  # ValueError: 0.9 is not a valid value for color
findings.expected: A bare RGB(A) tuple treated as one color broadcast to every dataset, or an error that names the list-wrapping workaround.
findings.actual: ValueError: color= was given as a list/tuple of length 3, but there are 1 dataset(s) to plot; pass either a single value (broadcast to every dataset) or a list/tuple of length 1.  |  3 datasets: ValueError: 0.9 is not a valid value for color: supported inputs are (r, g, b) and (r, g, b, a) 0-1 float tuples; ...

findings.title: zlabel= text collides with the legend on matplotlib 3-D plots (both occupy the right margin)
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
d = lambda s: np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(s).randn(60,8),axis=0)
hyp.plot([d(1), d(2)], names=['subject 1','subject 2'], xlabel='PC1', ylabel='PC2', zlabel='PC3', save_path='collide.png', show=False)
findings.expected: zlabel and legend both readable without overlapping text.
findings.actual: Rendered PNG shows 'PC3' overlapping the legend's first entry (see w1_neuro_names_title_axes.png, right edge ~y=235-275); zlabel-only and legend-only control images have no overlap.

findings.title: show= docstring still claims 'the figure, axis and data objects will still be returned' (0.x return signature)
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0)
out = hyp.plot(A, show=False)
print(type(out))  # <class 'matplotlib.figure.Figure'> -- no axis/data objects returned
findings.expected: show= docstring matching the 1.0 return shape ('the Figure is still returned').
findings.actual: Docstring line: 'If set to False, the figure will not be displayed, but the figure, axis and data objects will still be returned (default: True).' Runtime: returns a bare matplotlib Figure.

findings.title: hue= + color= warning still says 'Using group, color keyword will be ignored' (stale kwarg name, garbled grammar)
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, warnings, hypertools as hyp
x = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(60,5),axis=0)
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    hyp.plot(x, '.', hue=['a']*30+['b']*30, color='red', show=False)
print([str(m.message) for m in w])
findings.expected: Warning naming the actual kwargs: hue= and color=.
findings.actual: warnings=['Using group, color keyword will be ignored.']

findings.title: All three alias warnings (color/colors, linestyle/linestyles, marker/markers) contain literal ~30-space runs
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, warnings, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0); B = A+1
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    hyp.plot([A,B], marker='o', markers=['s','^'], show=False)
print(repr(str(w[0].message)))
findings.actual: 'Both marker and markers defined: marker will be                               ignored in favor of markers.'

findings.title: names= accepts a bare string and silently splits it into characters
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0); B = A+1
fig = hyp.plot([A,B], names='ab', show=False)
print([t.get_text() for t in fig.axes[0].get_legend().get_texts()])  # ['a','b']
findings.expected: TypeError/ValueError explaining names= takes a list of per-dataset names.
findings.actual: names='ab' (bare str, 2 datasets) -> legend ['a', 'b'] (silently split into chars)

findings.title: legend= accepts a bare string (undocumented) and broadcasts it into N identical legend entries
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0); B = A+1
fig = hyp.plot([A,B], legend='groups', show=False)
print([t.get_text() for t in fig.axes[0].get_legend().get_texts()])  # ['groups','groups']
findings.expected: Error, deduplication, or documented behavior for a scalar-string legend; wrong-length error should say legend= not label=.
findings.actual: legend='groups' -> legend entries ['groups', 'groups'] ; wrong length -> ValueError: label= was given as a list/tuple of length 1, but there are 2 dataset(s) to plot; ...

findings.title: labels= length mismatch is silently accepted despite docstring 'Must be dimensionality of data (x)'
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0)
hyp.plot(A, labels=['only-one-label'], show=False)  # no error, 1 annotation
hyp.plot(A, labels=['L%d'%i for i in range(50)], show=False)  # no error, 30 annotations
findings.expected: ValueError mirroring hue='s: 'labels has 1 entry but the data has 30 observations...'
findings.actual: labels len 1 vs 30 points: NO error; 1 annotations drawn: ['only-one-label'] | labels len 50 vs 30 points: NO error; 30 annotations drawn

findings.title: size= is not validated up front: malformed values crash after the full pipeline with errors that never name size=
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0)
hyp.plot(A, size='big', show=False)   # ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)
hyp.plot(A, size=[8], show=False)     # ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)
findings.expected: Fail-fast ValueError naming size= ('size= must be a [width, height] pair in inches; got ...') before the pipeline runs.
findings.actual: ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)  /  ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)  (from matplotlib figure.py:3139 via matplotlib_backend.py:2176 fig.set_size_inches(size))

findings.title: explore= (and animation dimensionality) misuse raises AssertionError instead of ValueError
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0)
hyp.plot(A, ndims=2, explore=True, show=False)
findings.expected: ValueError('explore=True is only supported for 3-D static plots; pass ndims=3 ...').
findings.actual: AssertionError: Explore mode is currently only supported for 3D plots.

findings.title: Non-numeric elev=/azim= accepted silently; crash deferred to draw/save time with a cryptic numpy error
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.cumsum(np.random.RandomState(1).randn(30,5),axis=0)
fig = hyp.plot(A, elev='up', show=False)  # no error here
fig.savefig('/tmp/x.png')  # TypeError: ufunc 'deg2rad' not supported...
findings.expected: Fail-fast ValueError naming elev=/azim= as numbers in degrees.
findings.actual: plot() succeeds; savefig raises: TypeError: ufunc 'deg2rad' not supported for the input types, and the inputs could not be safely coerced to any supported types according to the casting rule ''safe''

findings.title: ax= given a non-Axes object fails with cryptic AttributeError ('str' object has no attribute 'name')
findings.repro:
